objective: Determine why every role title in older D011 and D166 snapshots is absent from current canonical role records, using external task evidence and the current domain area boundaries.

authority_and_scope.method: Compare normalized title identity, inspect title aliases, source-backed domain/area boundaries, official occupational task profiles, and relevant current industry roles. Titles remain out of active routes unless a task-specific route meets both the domain and an existing area boundary.
authority_and_scope.no_role_data_mutation: This audit resolves historical title mismatches and records source-backed route candidates. It does not change the current canonical role library or area routes.

disposition_rule: A title is not retained merely because the general occupation operates in finance, engineering, manufacturing, or autonomous technology. Keep it only where source-backed tasks fit the domain and at least one existing area. Use explicit task conditions for broad occupations. Do not turn product-adjacency or sector employment into an area route.

D011.legacy_aliases: auditor  ·  finance auditor  ·  internal auditor  ·  audit manager  ·  chartered accountant
D011.decision: General financial statement, compliance and control audits are not the same work as quantitative model validation; the legacy aliases are general auditor/internal auditor.
D011.source_finding: O*NET 13-2011.00 describes accounting records, statements, reporting standards, reconciliations, audit findings, internal controls and tax compliance. It is a general accounting/audit occupation, not quantitative financial pricing, market-risk modeling, or systematic investment work.

D011.legacy_aliases: budget and policy analyst  ·  budget accountant  ·  budget officer  ·  cost and planning analyst
D011.decision: Program/organizational budget analysis does not fit market-risk modeling, instrument pricing, or systematic investment/trading.
D011.source_finding: O*NET 13-2031.00 covers fiscal allocation, operating budgets, cost analysis, program resources, budget controls and cost-benefit analysis. Cost Analyst is among its reported titles. These tasks concern organizational/program budgets, not the three D011 area boundaries.

D011.legacy_aliases: fiscal advisor  ·  tax specialist  ·  tax expert  ·  tax evaluator  ·  tax preparer
D011.decision: Tax law interpretation, return preparation and client tax planning are separate from the D011 specialization areas.
D011.source_finding: O*NET 13-2082.00 explicitly lists Tax Advisor among reported titles and describes tax return preparation, tax law, deductions, tax calculations and client tax planning.

D011.legacy_aliases: finance manager  ·  financial administrator  ·  accounting supervisor  ·  financial accountant  ·  accountant
D011.decision: Corporate finance control, accounting, budgeting, cash management and financial reporting do not establish one of the D011 specialization area tasks.
D011.source_finding: O*NET 11-3031.01 covers organization-level cash, reserves, budgeting, financial statements, investment of surpluses, accounting controls, procurement, tax and staff supervision. The role is corporate treasury/control rather than quantitative market modeling or financial engineering.

D011.legacy_aliases: finance accountant  ·  public finance officer  ·  treasury accountant  ·  treasury officer  ·  public finance manager
D011.decision: Public-sector accounting and treasury/budget administration do not establish quantitative financial engineering or market/investment modeling.
D011.source_finding: O*NET 13-2011.00 describes accounting records, statements, reporting standards, reconciliations, audit findings, internal controls and tax compliance. It is a general accounting/audit occupation, not quantitative financial pricing, market-risk modeling, or systematic investment work.

D011.legacy_aliases: quantity surveyor  ·  cost accountant  ·  cost accounting clerk  ·  cost recovery estimator  ·  cost and budget analyst
D011.decision: The snapshot aliases include cost accountant and cost/budget analyst; O*NET groups Cost Analyst under budget analysis. Product/program costing is not financial-instrument pricing.
D011.source_finding: O*NET 13-2031.00 covers fiscal allocation, operating budgets, cost analysis, program resources, budget controls and cost-benefit analysis. Cost Analyst is among its reported titles. These tasks concern organizational/program budgets, not the three D011 area boundaries.

D011.decision: Grant administration involves grant review, award, financial administration and compliance, not the D011 areas.
D011.source_finding: SAMHSA defines a Grant Management Officer's work as business management, review/negotiation/award/administration, compliance interpretation and authorizing grant expenditure. O*NET Fundraisers covers donor solicitation and funding proposals. Grant administration is not quantitative finance or financial engineering.

D011.legacy_aliases: fraud analyst  ·  fraud examiner  ·  fraud prevention analyst  ·  fraud investigations manager  ·  financial fraud investigator
D011.decision: Fraud investigation and evidence gathering may analyze financial data, but that does not equal quantitative market/investment modeling. A fraud-analytics role would require a distinct assigned task and area record.
D011.source_finding: O*NET 13-2099.04 describes evidence gathering, interviews, reporting and fraud investigation/prevention. Related task records include examining financial data for irregularities and designing fraud-detection tools; this is fraud examination/analytics, not quantitative finance unless a distinct financial-modeling assignment is evidenced.

D011.legacy_aliases: accounting systems analyst  ·  accounts analyst  ·  accounting specialist  ·  accounting methods analyst

D011.source_finding: O*NET 13-2011.00 describes accounting records, statements, reporting standards, reconciliations, audit findings, internal controls and tax compliance. It is a general accounting/audit occupation, not quantitative financial pricing, market-risk modeling, or systematic investment work.

D011.legacy_aliases: audit checker  ·  auditing supervisor  ·  audit leader  ·  audit inspector  ·  audit examiner

D011.source_finding: O*NET 13-2011.00 describes accounting records, statements, reporting standards, reconciliations, audit findings, internal controls and tax compliance. D011.legacy_aliases: insolvency practitioner  ·  insolvency trustee  ·  bankruptcy analyst  ·  trustees in bankruptcy  ·  trustee in bankruptcy

D011.source_finding: U.S. Courts describes bankruptcy trustee duties as administering/reorganizing an estate, accounting for property, reviewing claims and court reporting. This is insolvency administration, not an area in D011.

D011.legacy_aliases: dividends clerk  ·  dividend and coupon analyst  ·  dividend calculation clerk  ·  dividends analyst  ·  dividend clerk
D011.disposition: exclude_from_D011_legacy_identity; require a distinct task-qualified role for investment work
D011.decision: Snapshot aliases and current employer evidence primarily indicate dividend/coupon processing and accounting. The ESCO-derived record also mentions stock valuation/forecasting, so the title is ambiguous. Keep this old identity out of D011; route a separately evidenced dividend-yield researcher/quantitative equity analyst only when the actual job forecasts/value securities and develops investment strategies.
D011.source_finding: The snapshot's aliases include dividend clerk and dividend/coupon analyst. An ESCO-derived profile describes dividend calculation, recordkeeping and payment work, while a current Scotiabank capital-markets posting describes corporate-actions processing, reconciliations, exception queues and payment readiness. Neither supports a D011 quantitative investment route by title alone. A separately documented role that forecasts dividends, values securities and builds a systematic equity strategy could support the systematic-investment area, but it is a different, task-qualified role identity.

D011.source_finding: O*NET 13-2011.00 describes accounting records, statements, reporting standards, reconciliations, audit findings, internal controls and tax compliance. O*NET directly includes this reported title under Robotics Engineers and lists autonomous-vehicle design, automatic vehicle control, advanced sensing, sensor-data processing, computer vision and robotic-system integration. This establishes a conditional D166 role fit when the person's assignment is the road-vehicle ADS stack.

Retain in D166 only when the assignment develops/integrates autonomous-vehicle powertrain controls or interfaces; the current Powertrain Engineer role is the closer canonical role. The source-backed D166 role is an autonomous powertrain systems/integration assignment; the generic Engine Designer title is not equivalent and should not be a separate route unless that condition is met. Current Powertrain Engineer is the closer canonical role family.

new_role_candidates_discovered.route_condition: Role assignment integrates road-vehicle ADS hardware/software, sensor networks, control interfaces or fleet test systems, and validates end-to-end system behavior.
new_role_candidates_discovered.evidence_summary: NVIDIA's Vehicle Integration Engineer posting covers integration of AV subsystems into vehicle E/E architecture, cross-stack debug, test-fleet build/sign-off and component validation. Mobileye lists Autonomous Vehicle System Integrator work in hardware/software bring-up, sensor/computing/network integration and system validation.
